1343f02fe892f184.text: Version 2.0 changed several names. The old names were deprecated in 1.8 and removed in 2.0. max_retries was renamed to retries. It now accepts an int or a strand.Retry.

1343f02fe892f184.text: It now accepts an int or a strand.Retry. Retry(method_whitelist=...) was renamed to Retry(allowed_methods=...). Timeout.total used to default to 60 seconds. It now defaults to None.

1343f02fe892f184.text: It now defaults to None. strand.ConnectTimeout and strand.ReadTimeout were merged into strand.TimeoutError. If you catch the old exceptions, catch strand.TimeoutError instead. Code that set max_retries=0 to turn retries off should now pass retries=False. Passing 0 still works but logs a warning.

17e5ed42c9f59c9d.text: Strand is a small HTTP client for Python. This page explains how it waits and when it tries again.

sentences.text: Strand is a small HTTP client for Python.
This page explains how it waits and when it tries again.

18e5004b0fafa3e5.text: Between two attempts Strand sleeps backoff_factor * 2 ** (attempt - 1) seconds. With the default factor of 0.5 that is approx. 0.5 s, 1 s and 2 s. The sleep never exceeds Retry.max_backoff, which is 120 seconds by default.

sentences.text: Between two attempts Strand sleeps backoff_factor * 2 ** (attempt - 1) seconds.
With the default factor of 0.5 that is approx. 0.5 s, 1 s and 2 s.
The sleep never exceeds Retry.max_backoff, which is 120 seconds by default.

18e5004b0fafa3e5.text: If the server sends a Retry-After header, Strand waits that long instead. Values over max_backoff are capped. Set respect_retry_after=False to ignore the header.

sentences.text: If the server sends a Retry-After header, Strand waits that long instead.

Set respect_retry_after=False to ignore the header.

28cdc1d58dcbfa9e.text: Every request has a timeout. By default Strand waits 10 seconds for the connection and 30 seconds for the response, i.e. a slow server fails after at most 40 seconds in total.

sentences.text: Every request has a timeout.
By default Strand waits 10 seconds for the connection and 30 seconds for the response, i.e. a slow server fails after at most 40 seconds in total.

28cdc1d58dcbfa9e.text: Pass a strand.Timeout object to change that, e.g. Timeout(connect=2.5, read=60). What happens when the timeout is reached? Strand raises strand.TimeoutError and closes the connection. The error is never retried unless you enable retries (see Retries).

28cdc1d58dcbfa9e.text: Example: A timeout of 0 is not allowed and raises ValueError. Use None to wait forever, which is almost never what you want in production.
